kept_not_a_defect.sub_item: insert_takeoffs validates every parent against rows that exist BEFORE the batch (iOS accepts a parent restored earlier in the same batch)
kept_not_a_defect.why: Not a Windows defect: Windows never restores a takeoff under its original uid (the writer allocates new uids), so a parent has to exist before the insert.

kept_not_a_defect.sub_item: drag validity (polygon_is_valid) evaluated on scene coordinates instead of OST coordinates
kept_not_a_defect.why: Not a practical defect: validity is decided on coordinates scaled by OST * 72 * view_scale / scale_ratio, so for exactly collinear or touching (degenerate) polygons the answer can depend on floating-point rounding of that scale factor.

kept_not_a_defect.sub_item: HTML export includes hidden-layer conditions (iOS filters them)
kept_not_a_defect.why: Not a defect: deliberate and test-pinned.

kept_not_a_defect.sub_item: export page and takeoff order follows the user's selection order (iOS sorts)
kept_not_a_defect.why: Not a defect: deliberate and pinned.

kept_not_a_defect.sub_item: LZX and Quantum cabinet compression (iOS decodes stored and MSZIP only)
kept_not_a_defect.why: Not a Windows problem.

kept_not_a_defect.sub_item: boolean columns: Windows writes the Access Yes/No true value (-1), iOS mixes 1 and -1
kept_not_a_defect.why: Not a Windows defect.

kept_not_a_defect.sub_item: per-page selected area (BidPageSettings.BidAreaSelected) and inactive-area colouring
kept_not_a_defect.why: Not a defect: a deliberate Windows feature (areas are surfaced there, not on iOS).

kept_not_a_defect.sub_item: iOS-only Connect, Tolerance, Snap-to-Linear controls (Windows has no UI for those columns)
kept_not_a_defect.why: Not a defect: the columns are part of the OST schema and Windows round-trips them untouched (its update writes only changed fields), it just has no UI for them.

kept_not_a_defect.sub_item: area meshes: Windows inward (negative signed volume), iOS outward
kept_not_a_defect.why: Not a separate defect: inward in-memory winding of the area, linear and count generators is the Windows convention (the OBJ writer's face swap and the Python flip after the boolean are built around it).

kept_not_a_defect.sub_item: flat quantized face shading on iOS instead of Windows' 60-degree crease-angle smooth shading
kept_not_a_defect.why: Not a Windows defect: crease-angle smooth shading is the intended Windows look; flat shading on iOS is a deliberate rendering-layer choice (PORTING_LOG 2026-03-23).

kept_not_a_defect.sub_item: curved linear takeoffs: no curved placement and no centre handle on iOS
kept_not_a_defect.why: Not a Windows defect: Windows supports curved linears (arc band, three handles, 6-value position); iOS scope decision only.

kept_not_a_defect.sub_item: camera refit on every empty-to-non-empty page selection on iOS; Windows keeps the camera within a bid
kept_not_a_defect.why: Not a Windows defect: the camera is fitted once per bid scene and kept across same-bid scene updates (pinned); the iOS transition refit is a deliberate iOS addition.

kept_not_a_defect.sub_item: note 1: placement left running when the Image layer is hidden
kept_not_a_defect.why: Only an edge case: a condition assigned to the Image layer is hidden and unplaceable after the Image layer is hidden, while the placement tool stays armed (neither suspended nor restored). Superseded / updated 2026-11-20 (job 5): iOS ported the exemption (single toggle only) and the tap guard, so iOS and Windows agree.

kept_not_a_defect.sub_item: whitespace-only Rise / Run: Windows rejects, old iOS accepted as 0
kept_not_a_defect.why: Not a defect: Windows rejects whitespace-only Rise and Run with 'Rise must be a number.' / 'Run must be a number.' (an empty field means 0).

kept_not_a_defect.sub_item: 'Count as Negative Quantity' acts on the plan-view selected takeoffs only
kept_not_a_defect.why: Not a defect: Windows changes only the takeoffs passed in (the plan-view selection) and pushes one local history entry; this is the behaviour the iOS code change copies.
